title: Vivary, step by step
introduction: A maintained guide for understanding the product, exploring how the parts connect, and reviewing design choices with their consequences.

review.authority: the submitted guide reply in the product conversation

acceptedRequirements.title: Multiple conversations within each project
acceptedRequirements.authority: Jeff's explicit correction in the product conversation
acceptedRequirements.explanation: A project can contain multiple independent chats. The workspace shows one selected conversation in the center at a time. Each conversation has its own bounded context and can reach model context limits.
acceptedRequirements.implementationImpact: Navigation must let users start, select and return to several project conversations. Potentially concurrent thread activity needs visible status and approvals for each thread, plus controls for conflicting edits to shared files. The current runtime permits one active root conversation run at a time. This remains an explicit implementation limitation until concurrency support lands.

acceptedRequirements.title: Harness-owned capabilities with observed availability
acceptedRequirements.authority: Jeff's explicit correction in the product conversation
acceptedRequirements.explanation: The selected supported installed harness owns its tools, MCP configuration, models and native permission semantics. Vivary displays actual observed availability, preserves unknown states and does not add a second general tool picker.
acceptedRequirements.implementationImpact: Vivary keeps project and host authorization plus approval, denial and Stop for the exact request. It provides the original engine and narrow deterministic workspace operations. Before adding another tool, explain whether a missing capability is blocked by the harness, observed host state, authorization or an existing Vivary operation.

acceptedRequirements.title: Offline templates with optional source links later
acceptedRequirements.authority: Jeff's explicit correction in the product conversation
acceptedRequirements.explanation: Templates start as an offline baseline. A later optional community collection can use the existing vivary-site to point at source GitHub repositories and downloads. It is not a marketplace or a separate template site.
acceptedRequirements.implementationImpact: Show a preview before apply. Treat downloads as inert until a separately authorized operation applies them. Downloading a template never implies execution.

tour.title: Choose your project
tour.plain: Open the project you want to work on, then choose one of its conversations. The project can hold several independent chats alongside its files, even if the folder later moves.
tour.why: You should not have to remember which window or agent owns your work, or force unrelated work through one context window.
tour.detail: Stable project identity is separate from the current authorized root. Registration does not modify or adopt the folder. If a saved managed folder loses verified access, its project and conversation history remain attached to the same IDs. Review connection explains the recorded folder and consequences; only an explicit reviewed reconnect can restore access to that same managed folder. Canceling changes nothing, and reconnecting neither edits files nor starts an agent. Only a single recorded managed-folder binding is eligible for this recovery. An uncertain result keeps the exact reviewed retry through another review. After a reload, Review connection can find a recorded but unfinished reconnection without changing files and offer Finish reconnecting. A newly changed folder gets a fresh plan. External folders or multiple bindings need a separate path.

tour.title: Return to the conversation
tour.plain: Return to an existing conversation or start another inside the same project. Each chat has separate history and model context.
tour.why: A long project needs more than one context window, and separate work should not blur into one transcript.
tour.detail: The center shows one selected conversation at a time, not the project's only conversation. Existing Native thread, Code and harness records retain their own identities. A conversation can reach its model context limit. Another chat starts with a separate context. Potentially concurrent work needs status and approvals for each thread plus controls for conflicting edits to shared files. The current runtime still permits one active root conversation run at a time. Unsent drafts belong to the current client and profile; this does not promise draft transfer to another device. Project-bound Native persistence is integrated. Codex follow-ups resume its recorded native session. Per-conversation draft restoration across restarts remains issue #9 acceptance.

tour.title: Choose a harness and model
tour.plain: New conversations select Claude Code or Codex. Codex reports its available subscription models. The broader unified harness catalog and linked switching flow remain planned.
tour.why: You can see the harness's actual available capabilities without configuring a second general tool picker or a predefined persona.
tour.detail: Target behavior, not an available switching flow: A different harness creates a linked conversation. The source history stays available, while the material supplied to the new model is shown separately. Linking sends nothing. An installed CLI needs a registered, compatible adapter and readiness checks before it can run. Unknown availability stays unknown. Vivary retains project and host authorization plus approval, denial and Stop.

tour.title: Approve or decline work
tour.plain: Codex Send starts immediately. Review native action requests when its selected permission mode requires a decision. Approval, denial and Stop remain reachable.
tour.why: Background work must be visible and understandable.
tour.detail: Approval remains bound to the originating request and Native owner. A changed request or scope needs revalidation. Runtime completion is separate from verified acceptance. Normal, Read only, and YOLO apply to the next turn. Denying one action does not imply the model never started. Active work retains its captured mode.

tour.title: Open a file when you need it
tour.plain: Read the formatted document beside the conversation. Choose Edit to change it, or expand it for focused work.
tour.why: Inspecting a file should not interrupt the conversation or lose a draft.
tour.detail: The editor uses existing scoped read/save/rename actions. A changed disk version produces a recoverable conflict. Viewing a file does not send it to a model.

tour.title: Leave a useful continuation record
tour.plain: Ask the agent to update the handoff when you need a written account of the work, evidence and next step.
tour.why: A future conversation should have a useful starting point.
tour.detail: Code can detect stale coverage without a model call. Writing a fresh narrative is separate agent work. Preparing a handoff never auto-cleans, commits, merges or deletes files.

M01: Keeps the selected conversation central and lets you open or close supporting panels.
M02: Keeps projects distinct and checks which folder is available and authorized. A workspace content preview does not grant folder access.
M03: Lets each project hold several independent chats, return to earlier work and follow links without rewriting history.
M04: The target adapter catalog displays observed capabilities from supported installed harnesses. The grouped model picker and linked switching remain planned.
M05: Checks permissions and keeps approval, denial and Stop attached to the correct work.
M06: Reads and edits project documents while preserving drafts and handling changed files.
M07: Set up and operate a workspace
Uses the original Vivary engine. The shared creator's target-bound five-file preview, greenfield apply, and no-write exact retry passed bundled and hosted checks. Existing-folder apply remains open.
M08: Finds files, conversation content and sourced facts within the right project.
M09: Shows intended work and dependencies from the selected task source. A creator file-content plan controls one workspace change without replacing that task owner.
M10: Do, check and hand over work
Coordinates bounded work, reviews actual results and prepares continuation records.
M11: Connects supported Git or other workflows without requiring them for every project.
M12: Produces sourced material and keeps suggested lessons separate from accepted changes.
M13: Handles later inbox and maintenance flows with explicit routing, limits and authority.
M14: Coordinates the desktop, private browser connection and supported project preview.
M15: Prepares verified releases and later public integrations through their approval gates.
M16: Makes actual evidence, limitations and contributor instructions easy to find.

decisions.title: Project details on a wide desktop
decisions.timing: Accepted for the first interface slice

accepted.authority: Jeff's submitted review of guide snapshot e86d06ed592a2d3c

decisions.explanation: Keep the conversation spacious. Project identity, activity and urgent recovery stay in the header. Open details when you want them.
decisions.impact: The first workspace slice starts with project details closed on wide desktop. The header keeps essential identity, activity, recovery, approval and Stop visible. The full details panel remains available on request.

options.label: Header first
options.tradeoff: More conversation space. One click to inspect full project details.

options.label: Compact details panel open
options.tradeoff: More information immediately visible. Uses some horizontal space.

decisions.title: Handoff-update timing

accepted.authority: Jeff's submitted review of guide snapshot e86d06ed592a2d3c

decisions.explanation: Show when the handoff is out of date. Updating its narrative is agent work, with the applicable approval policy.
decisions.impact: Vivary marks stale coverage without a model call. It updates the handoff narrative only when the user requests it. A future project may propose named checkpoints through a separate explicit opt-in.

options.label: Manual by default
options.tradeoff: You request each update. The stale indicator updates without a model call.

options.label: Optional named checkpoints
options.tradeoff: Explicit project opt-in to defined updates inside an authorized workflow.
